title: Nurse who 'died' claims he saw 'something he wasn't meant to' in afterlife
excerpt: Former emergency room nurse Jack Allen says he experienced an overwhelming feeling of love during a near-fatal wasp sting in Mexico — an ordeal that changed how he views life and death
content:
Former emergency room nurse Jack Allen says he experienced an overwhelming feeling of love during a near-fatal wasp sting in Mexico — an ordeal that changed how he views life and death

15:20, 30 Oct 2026

A former emergency room nurse says a near-fatal wasp sting left him in a place in the afterlife that felt like home— and changed the way he thinks about death.

‌

‌

Jack Allen, who is in his mid-50s and spent most of his life in Texas, became unresponsive after being stung on a ranch in Mexico in September 2024. He says his companions believed he had died, while he recalls being somewhere filled with colour, flowers and an overwhelming sense of love. "I closed my eyes that day on the dirt and I was instantly in another place and this is where it's hard to talk about," he said.

‌

Sharing his account in a video, Jack became visibly emotional as he described the experience. He hopes his story will comfort others who have been through something similar. He said: "I've gotten better at it, but a lot of times when I recall this, I become physically emotional. And it's because of the intense feeling, overwhelming feeling of love that I felt there. It was immense."

‌

Jack said the garden had lush green grass, beautiful flowers and fruit. It felt familiar, as though he had been there before, and gave him a powerful sense of being home. He also recalled feeling that he suddenly understood time and space.

In his account, his wife appeared youthful and full of vitality, without the foot disability she had in everyday life. Surrounded by brightness and vivid colours, he said he felt a love unlike anything he had known before. "I never felt more in love with her ever than I ever have before," he recalled.

‌

They walked through the garden gathering flowers until she apologised and told him he had to "go back". Jack said: "And at that moment I would have done anything she asked. I was in such a state of emotional bliss. And boom. I feel a sucking feeling real quick. And then my eyes open and I'm laying on the ground in the dirt and my friends start panicking. They're yelling. And I can honestly say I have never felt better in my life as I did at that very moment."

The ordeal began while Jack was working on his tropical fruit ranch in Mexico, where he had moved intending to retire after 37 years as an emergency room nurse.

‌

Accompanied by his business partner and two ranchers, he struck a hanging branch with a machete, disturbing a large wasps' nest at the other end. He tried to flee but was stung on the shoulder.

‌

His companions identified the insect as an "executioner wasp". Jack said he became lightheaded and his heart rate dropped sharply, prompting him to lower himself to the ground and close his eyes.

According to his account of what his companions later told him, his eyes rolled back, he convulsed and became unresponsive. They poured water on him and slapped his face in an attempt to revive him.

‌

"I have no memory of this, but apparently it was terrifying. And they did that for about two minutes and then they realized I was dead. And, you know, my partner tells me that all that was going through his head was, 'What are we going to tell his wife and son?'"

When he regained consciousness, Jack reassured his friends that he was fine. But the relief was short-lived: within less than a minute, he said his blood pressure plummeted, his heart rate soared and he could not lift his head from the ground.

‌

He survived and said he wept the following morning as he remembered the love he felt during what he believes was an encounter with the afterlife. Coming to terms with the experience was difficult, but he said it taught him not to take anything for granted.

‌

"I learned a lot of things," he said. "I saw things that maybe I wasn't intended to and shouldn't have, maybe we're not intended to see this on earth because this is our test. This is how we learn. I feel we're here because we choose to be here. We all choose to be here."

Jack said he later lost his ranch in a hurricane, saw his business collapse and went through a divorce, before having to sell his Texas property.

‌

As he rebuilds his life, he says he has returned to caring for and supporting others. He believes there is a purpose behind his survival and wants to make the most of his remaining time.

His years in emergency and critical care had exposed him to thousands of deaths, he said, but his outlook is now different. He explained: "I can tell you lots of different experiences of watching people die before me. I look at it totally differently now and I feel happy for these people now."

Recalling the death of a friend in Mexico, he added: "I didn't cry over that. So yes, it's changed me. I had a good friend when I was in Mexico after this happened and my wife at the time called me and told me that he had passed away in his sleep, probably a heart attack. He had a bad heart and my attitude was like, 'Ah, way to go buddy. You did, you did it man. Congratulations. Congratulations my friend.'"
